payload.prompt: Um dos seus clientes tem uma fatura vencida. Encontre a fatura vencida e registe uma taxa de lembrete de 70 NOK. Debito contas a receber (1500), credito receitas de lembrete (3400). Também crie uma fatura para a taxa de lembrete ao cliente e envie-a. Além disso, registe um pagamento parcial de 5000 NOK na fatura vencida.

payload.goal: Find the overdue customer invoice, add a reminder fee of 70 NOK via accounting entry and customer invoice, send the reminder-fee invoice, and register a partial payment of 5000 NOK on the overdue invoice.
success_checks: An overdue customer invoice is identified.
A voucher is created debiting 1500 and crediting 3400 for 70 NOK.
A customer invoice for 70 NOK reminder fee is created for the same customer.
A payment of 5000 NOK is registered against the overdue invoice.
Outstanding balance on the overdue invoice is reduced by 5000 NOK.
risk_notes: No specific overdue invoice or customer is identified in the prompt; selection criteria may be ambiguous if multiple overdue invoices exist.
Sandbox is empty, so prerequisite customer/order/invoice data may need to be created before payment registration can be demonstrated.
Sending an invoice requires a valid customer delivery method such as email; none provided.
Reminder fee VAT is not specified; may be exempt or require specific treatment depending on accounting policy, so VAT is uncertain.
Registering payment normally requires payment date and bank/cash account context; not provided.
Creating both a voucher and a reminder-fee invoice for the same fee may duplicate accounting impact unless intended workflow is confirmed.
payload.suggested_first_action: List customer invoices and identify the overdue unpaid invoice to determine the target customer and invoice ID.
ordered_steps: GET /invoices?status=OPEN to find overdue invoices and select invoice with dueDate before today
GET /invoices/{invoiceId} to confirm customer, remaining amount, and overdue status
If sandbox has no bank account: create/setup bank account required for payment registration
If customer does not exist in sandbox: POST /customers to create the customer from the selected invoice context
POST /vouchers with lines: debit account 1500 amount 70 NOK, credit account 3400 amount 70 NOK, linked to customer if supported
POST /orders for the customer with one order line: Reminder fee, quantity 1, unit price 70 NOK, VAT as configured/confirmed
POST /orders/{orderId}/invoice to create the reminder-fee invoice
POST /payments or /invoices/{invoiceId}/payments to register partial payment of 5000 NOK on the overdue invoice
GET /invoices/{invoiceId} to verify remaining balance reduced by 5000 NOK
GET /invoices/{reminderInvoiceId} to verify reminder-fee invoice exists and is sent

rules: For bank account setup: isBankAccount=true, bankAccountNumber='12345678903', bankAccountCountry={"id": 161}.
MUST include id and version from the GET response.
When email is provided, ALWAYS set BOTH email AND invoiceEmail to the same value.
Do NOT send isCustomer (it's readOnly and auto-set).
For addresses, use postalAddress={addressLine1, postalCode, city, country={id: 161}} for Norway.
ALWAYS search first if product_number is provided: GET /product?number=<number> — sandbox pre-seeds products.
Only POST /product if GET returns 0 results.
Use 'number' field for the product number (NOT productNumber).
priceExcludingVat sets the base price. Also set vatType={"id": 3|5|6}.
Requires customer={"id": customer_id}.
Set orderDate and deliveryDate (use today_iso from execution_brief).
When a product was created, ALWAYS include product={"id": product_id} on the orderline.
Use unitPriceExcludingVatCurrency for the price field.
Set vatType={"id": 3} for 25%, {"id": 5} for 15%, {"id": 6} for 0%.
For multiple lines, prefer POST /order/orderline/list for efficiency.
Pass orders=[{"id": order_id}] to link order.
Set invoiceDate and invoiceDueDate.
Bank account 1920 MUST be configured first (see bank account setup pattern).
Method is PUT, not POST.
All params are QUERY PARAMETERS: paymentDate, paymentTypeId, paidAmount or paidAmountCurrency.
Get paymentTypeId first via GET /invoice/paymentType.
Method is PUT, not POST.
date is a QUERY PARAMETER: PUT /ledger/voucher/{id}/:reverse?date=YYYY-MM-DD
Do NOT send date in the request body.

payload.headline: Half the checks failed: payment, invoice send, and likely voucher details incorrect
what_went_wrong: Check 4 failed: PUT /invoice/2147632676/:payment likely missing required params (paymentTypeId, amount=5000, paymentDate) — the call was made with no body/params visible in trace.
Check 5 failed: Invoice send (PUT /invoice/2147632749/:send) may have failed silently or lacked required sendType param, causing the send check to fail.
Check 6 failed: Possibly the reminder fee invoice or voucher posting details (account IDs, amounts, or currency linkage) did not satisfy the scorer's exact field requirements.
Semantic blocker triggered (1 error) on the orderline POST, causing a retry delay and indicating the enforcer flagged the 10000 NOK amount as suspicious despite it being necessary.
what_worked: Voucher creation with debit 1500 / credit 3400 for 70 NOK passed checks 1-3 correctly.
Customer, order, and overdue invoice setup was logically sound with past due date.
what_to_try_next: For PUT /invoice/:payment, explicitly include query params: paymentTypeId, amount=5000, paymentDate, and possibly paidToAccountId to ensure the payment registers correctly.
For PUT /invoice/:send, include sendType=EMAIL (or the correct enum) as a query parameter to ensure the send action is properly recorded by the scorer.
Verify the voucher postings use the correct sign convention (positive debit on 1500, negative credit on 3400) and include all required fields like vatType or currency that the scorer may validate.
unnecessary_calls: GET /ledger/account called 3 separate times — could be batched into one call with account number filters.
POST /order for reminder fee could potentially be skipped if a direct invoice POST supports line items without an order.
